questions.question_text: Which of these is an example of volatile memory?
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile because it loses its data when the power is turned off.

questions.question_text: Which of these is classified as volatile memory?
questions.explanation: Volatile memory, like RAM, requires power to maintain the stored information; it is cleared when the computer is turned off.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered volatile memory?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile because it loses all stored data when the power supply is turned off.

questions.question_text: What is the smallest unit of data in a computer?
questions.explanation: A 'bit' is a binary digit, representing either 0 or 1, and is the smallest unit of digital data.
